subject: Post-demo follow-up — private deploy peering, latency & test plan
messages:
From: David Liu <david.liu@clearmap.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearmap.io
Date: 2025-11-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo questions: private deploy peering & latency budget

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team appreciated the walkthrough of Redwood Private. A few follow-up items from our infra and SRE side so we can align acceptance criteria and schedule the hands-on validation: 

- Target workload: streaming chat where typical responses are 200–800 tokens. We expect bursts up to 1k tokens for a small subset of requests.
- Latency ask: Can you confirm expected tail/liveness numbers for streaming? Our initial requirement is p95 < 100ms end-to-end (ingress -> token stream to client) for 200–800 token responses. If you need to propose a different SLO for private deploys, please indicate trade-offs.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline 200 req/s sustained with peak concurrency ~50 sessions. We can scale up to 400 req/s for short bursts.
- Network topology: we're on AWS us-west-2, Transit Gateway + Direct Connect to our colo. We need pros/cons of peering (Direct Connect/PrivateLink) vs IPSEC VPN over Transit Gateway for RDW Private.
- Egress/NAT: we need to understand static egress IPs for allowlisting and whether redwood requires NAT to a managed egress or we can present fixed customer IPs.

We attached our network diagram. Two asks: can you (1) share a Mutual Action Plan with clear milestones for performance validation, and (2) propose the specific test harness and commands you want us to run (iperf/streaming smoke test). 

David
David Liu
Ops Lead, ClearMap
ops@clearmap.io

Attachment: clearmap_network_map.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: David Liu <david.liu@clearmap.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-14T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions: private deploy peering & latency budget

Thanks David — great questions and helpful diagram. Below is a concise recap plus proposed next steps (I'll keep items action-oriented so we can turn them into a short MAT).

Recap / Redwood baseline assumptions
- Typical streaming path (customer client -> customer LB -> transit -> Redwood Private gateway -> worker): we optimize for per-token emission and KV cache locality.
- Recommended SLO for private/VPC deployments (initial proposal): p50 ~ 40–60ms, p95 ~ 120–150ms, p99 ~ 300–400ms for 200–800 token responses under normal egress peering. Achieving p95 < 100ms is possible in controlled colo-to-colo peering with very low network RTT; if your path involves multiple cloud hops or NAT churn, we will need to validate.
- Throughput/concurrency: with a standard dedicated instance profile we can sustain 200 req/s with concurrency 50 using batching disabled for streaming-critical requests. We can provide burst capacity to 400 req/s for short periods, but this depends on worker sizing and your expected token-per-request distribution.

Action items / Proposed MAP (attached: mutual_action_plan_v0.1.docx)
1) Customer: Share IP blocks and egress NAT IPs + maintenance windows. (David)
2) Redwood: Share test harness (iperf commands + streaming smoke harness) and a short runbook for a 2-hour joint validation window. (Michael / Ben)
3) Joint: Run three tests — a) iperf/owamp for base RTT/jitter, b) sustained 15-minute throughput at target request size, c) 90-second streaming sessions to validate token emission tail. Capture p50/p95/p99 token delivery latency. (All)
4) Redwood: Provide a post-test results template and a recommended set of fallback policies (model variant + routing) if we see degraded tail latency. (Neha)

Quick notes on peering vs VPN
- Direct Connect/PrivateLink (preferred): lower jitter and consistent egress IPs for allowlisting; best path for hitting p95 targets.
- Transit Gateway + IPSEC VPN: operationally simpler but subject to RTT variability and NAT ephemeral ports; may require higher latency SLOs.

Attachments I've added for the run: sample_iperf_commands.txt (iperf3 with parallel streams + MTU notes) and the MAP v0.1. Ben — can you paste the iperf commands and the small script we use to wrap streaming sessions?

Proposed workshop window
- We're available Tue/Wed next week (11/18-11/19) 10:00–14:00 PST for a joint validation workshop. Please confirm who from your side will own the NAT/eDNS changes so we can coordinate allowlist cutovers.

Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v0.1.docx, sample_iperf_commands.txt

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, David Liu <david.liu@clearmap.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-15T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions: private deploy peering & latency budget

Quick follow from my side with concrete acceptance criteria we can validate during the workshop: 

Validation checklist (measurable):
- Network: RTT (client -> worker) p50 < 10ms, p95 < 30ms; jitter < 10ms for 95% of samples (iperf/owamp).
- Tail token delivery: for 200–800 token responses, streaming p95 per-token latency (time between token generation and network emit to client) < 150ms. If ClearMap needs p95 <100ms we should treat that as a stretch goal and record the path characteristics if missed.
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s for 15 min with <=5% error rate; spike to 400 req/s for 2 min acceptable.
- Concurrency: exercise 50 concurrent streaming sessions for 10 min to capture KV cache hit/miss behavior.
- Egress: static NAT IP(s) provided and confirmed in firewall rules; if you cannot provide static IPs we need to test with our managed egress and confirm allowlist steps.
- Observability: customer must provide access to flow logs / VPC flow sample or equivalent; Redwood will provide per-token latency traces and an artifacts bundle after the run.

I will own the post-test analysis and provide a results dashboard template. Ben — I'll need the small wrapper script you mentioned (to orchestrate streaming sessions and save timing traces).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: (none)

From: David Liu <david.liu@clearmap.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearmap.io, amanda.cho@clearmap.io
Date: 2025-11-18T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions: private deploy peering & latency budget

Thanks Michael & Neha — this is excellent and actionable. We can: 
- Provide static egress IPs from our Direct Connect path (I will confirm ranges by EOD Monday).
- Schedule the workshop for Wed 11/19 10:00–12:00 PST; Amanda Cho (SRE) will join and owns the VPC updates.
- We can run the iperf baseline and upload the results to the shared Drive prior to the workshop.

Two quick asks: please include the exact test harness repo or script location in the MAP so our SREs can review ahead of time, and confirm whether Redwood requires any firewall changes to accept incoming debug traces during the test window.

If that all looks good, we'll mark the MAP items as owner-assigned and move procurement gating forward (legal has a few questions but procurement isn't blocking the validation).

David
Ops Lead, ClearMap
